$schema_note: DERIVED — regenerate with tools/rule_presence_1835.py; tools/check.sh re-derives it and fails on drift. Do not hand-edit: every row's tier is a function of the dated readings its card carries.
the_rule: An attested or inferred resident is in the town's population unless there is EVIDENCE they were not — a documented departure, a dated appearance elsewhere, a source that places them outside. `uncertain` with no tier and no contrary reading is not that evidence. The owner, 2026-09-19: "if they are attested that's ideal if we know them already", and "I want a full population of the city to work from".

the_tier_is_derived.on_the_day: attested — a dated reading of this person whose window contains 1 July 1835.
the_tier_is_derived.spans: inferred — a cited source's own span runs through the day.
the_tier_is_derived.bracketed: inferred — the corpus reads this person at Chicago on both sides of the day.
the_tier_is_derived.carried: reconstructed — the corpus stops before the day; the project's standing rule carries the presence and the persistence model prices it.

the_floor: T-1172's R1 leg re-ruled every `uncertain` presence at tier `reconstructed`. 142 of these 820 rulings land ABOVE that on their own dated readings, which is what acceptance 3 asks for: an attested or inferred person never takes a presence tier below what their own evidence supports. A card graded `attested` whose last reading falls before the day keeps its attested RESIDENCE and takes a `reconstructed` PRESENCE — the two are different claims, and calling the presence inferred there would be the undeclared flip this stage refuses.
nothing_is_drawn_here: T-1172 drew against the persistence model and ruled 37 cards `absent` on the losing side. This stage does not draw: an absence with no evidence under it is not a finding, and the two evidenced absences below are the shape of a correct exclusion. `basis.kind` is `rule` and a rule owes no seed.

persistence_model.used_for: pricing a `carried` ruling, never for deciding one

evidenced_absences.name: The Porthier household
evidenced_absences.note: T-0478 resolves the earlier uncertainty. Pioneer History of Milwaukee dates Joseph Porthier leaving Chicago with Horace Chase on February 27, 1835; after a brief return to Chicago for means, Porthier left again March 21 and reached Milwaukee March 23. That dated migration is before the July 1 scene date.

evidenced_absences.name: The Wolcott household — a name the town's own records carry
evidenced_absences.note: THE RECORD PLACES THIS PERSON NOWHERE ON THE DAY, BECAUSE HE WAS DEAD. The old settlers' obituary dates the death 25 October 1830, before the scene date of 1 July 1835, and no record that places a person at Chicago names this one after it. A DEATH NOTICE IS NOT A PRESENCE (T-1131): the old settlers' obituary declares `places_in_1835: false` on every record it publishes, because its own header admits it prints citizens who arrived after 1843. It dates a death; it never says the man was standing in the town on 1 July 1835 — so it cannot be the at-or-before leg of a bracket, and a later source on the far side cannot close one over a dead man. `absent` and not `uncertain`: a silence is somewhere the sources have not looked, and a death is not a silence.
